article.excerpt: Motion Control lets you show the AI what you want instead of describing it. Combined with Nano Banana Pro's image quality, you get precise control over both appearance and movement.

content_sections.heading: Opening Hook
content_sections.content:
Most AI video tools force you to describe movement in words. "Make her dance gracefully" becomes a guessing game between you and the model. Motion Control flips this: you *show* the AI what you want by uploading a reference video. Combined with Nano Banana Pro's image quality, you get precise control over both appearance and movement.

The counterintuitive insight? **Success isn't about finding the perfect action clip — it's about choosing the right mode.**

content_sections.heading: Direct Answer
content_sections.content: Nano Banana Pro creates high-quality character images inside 11 Labs. Kling 2.6 Motion Control then transfers movements from any reference video onto that image. The key decision is choosing between Match Image mode (preserves character details, max 10 seconds) or Match Video mode (copies exact motion, max 30 seconds). Text prompts are optional — they control background and lighting, not the actual movement.

points.title: Match Image (10s)
points.description: prioritizes character consistency — textures and facial features stay true to your original image, but the AI may invent camera movements

points.title: Match Video (30s)
points.description: prioritizes motion accuracy — exact skeletal movement is copied, but character proportions may stretch to fit

points.title: Text prompts are optional
points.description: the reference video dictates all action; prompts only affect background and lighting

points.title: Generate reference videos internally
points.description: create a neutral-pose character in Nano Banana Pro, then animate it with Kling 2.6 to build your own motion library

dimensions.title: The Complete Workflow
dimensions.content: Start by creating your character in Nano Banana Pro at 2K resolution. Upload a reference photo, describe the scene (outfit, setting, pose), and generate multiple options. Pick your favorite, then switch to video mode. Select Kling 2.6 Motion Control, drag your image in, upload a motion reference video, and generate.

dimensions.title: Match Image vs Match Video — How to Choose
dimensions.content: Use Match Image when the character's look matters more than perfect motion replication. Use Match Video when you need exact movements and can tolerate minor character distortion.

dimensions.title: Prompt Strategy
dimensions.content: Here's what surprises most users: prompts don't control movement. When you add text to Motion Control, it affects scene elements — background details, lighting atmosphere, environmental context. The reference video handles *all* motion. Many creators leave prompts blank and see no difference in output quality.

dimensions.title: Common Pitfalls to Avoid
dimensions.content:
**Restrictive starting poses**: If your character image has arms crossed or an unusual stance, the AI struggles to map different movements onto it. Start with a neutral pose — arms by sides, centered framing.

**No reference video?** Create one. Generate a simple figure in Nano Banana Pro with neutral pose, switch to Kling 2.6, and prompt movements like "do a little tango dance" or "slowly walk backwards." Use these generated videos as motion references for your actual character images.

content_sections.heading: Why It Works
content_sections.content: Motion Control separates two problems that text-to-video muddles together: *what something looks like* and *how it moves*. Nano Banana Pro handles appearance with high-fidelity image generation. The reference video handles motion through direct visual specification. This division of labor means less guessing, fewer wasted generations, and results that match your creative intent.

content_sections.heading: How to Try It
steps: **Generate your character** in 11 Labs using Nano Banana Pro (select 2K, generate 4 options)
**Find or create a reference video** — either record yourself or generate one with Kling 2.6 from a neutral-pose image
**Switch to Kling 2.6 Motion Control** — drag in your character image and motion video
**Choose your mode** — Match Image for appearance priority, Match Video for motion priority — then generate

questions.question: Do I need a text prompt for Motion Control?
questions.answer: No. Prompts are optional and only affect background/lighting. The reference video controls all movement. Many users leave prompts blank.

questions.question: Can I create my own reference videos without filming?
questions.answer: Yes. Generate a neutral-pose character in Nano Banana Pro, then use Kling 2.6 (not Motion Control) to animate it with a text prompt describing the movement you want. Save that video as your motion reference.

questions.question: Which mode should I use if I'm unsure?
questions.answer: Start with Match Image for shorter clips where character consistency matters. Switch to Match Video if you need longer duration or precise motion matching and can accept some character distortion.

content_sections.heading: Source & Boundary
content_sections.content: This guide synthesizes the official 11 Labs workflow demonstrated in the referenced video. Results may vary based on image quality, reference video clarity, and the specific movements being transferred. Motion Control works best with single-character scenes and clear, unobstructed movements.
